subject: Incident: Hosted API elevated 503s — SprintBridge
messages:
From: Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@sprintbridge.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Elevated 503s observed on hosted API - affecting batch ingestion

Hi Vanessa —

We're seeing a spike of 503 responses from your hosted /v1/generate endpoint starting around 08:45 ET. It impacts our nightly ingestion job; ~30% of requests are returning 503 and retrying causes backoff saturation. Our SREs are throttling on our side but wanted to alert you as well in case this is platform-side.

Quick facts:
- Region: us-east-1
- Endpoint: api.redwood.ai/v1/generate (model: redwood-open-8b)
- First observed: ~08:45 ET
- Impact: Batch ingestion failing, delayed downstream jobs

Can you confirm if there are any active incidents on your side and if there's an ETA for mitigation?

Thanks,
Sophie Lee
SRE, SprintBridge

Hi Sophie — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the disruption. We're seeing increased 5xx rates aggregated in our telemetry for us-east-1 starting 08:40 ET and have opened an incident on our status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2025-06-18-503-surge.

What we're doing now:
- Triage in progress with infra and routing teams (assigned)
- Short-term mitigation: routing a portion of traffic to cold fallback pool to reduce pressure
- Monitoring for retry amplification — recommending you shorten retry windows temporarily if possible

I'll keep you in the loop and will share an initial timeline and any mitigations we turn on. Attaching a lightweight runbook summary as we triage (attachment stub).

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Elevated 503s observed on hosted API - affecting batch ingestion

Internal update:

- Root signal: transient eviction of a subset of KV cache shards in us-east-1 causing repeated cold starts for long-context sessions. That caused elevated latencies and, under our backpressure heuristics, 503s to protect downstream capacity.
- Mitigation applied at 09:40 ET: forced warmup of affected cache shards and activation of an expanded prefetch window. We observed a drop in 5xx percentage from ~28% to ~7% in the next 25 minutes.
- Next steps: compute a precise timeline and export request-level traces for SprintBridge timeframe (08:30–09:30 ET).

I'll assemble the timeline CSV and send to Vanessa for customer attachment.

—Sean
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 12:30:00 -0400

Hi Sophie / Alex —

Quick operational update and ask:

What happened (short): KV cache shard evictions in us-east-1 created a burst of cold starts for long-context model sessions. To prevent system-wide overload we triggered protective 503 responses under our circuit-breaker policy.

What we did:
- Forced warmup and expanded prefetch window for affected shards (09:40 ET)
- Scoped routing to reduce pressure on the most impacted pools (09:45 ET)
- Enabled a short-term capacity burst while we rebuild steady-state warm caches (09:55–11:10 ET)

Impact observed: improved from ~28% 5xx down to ~4–8% by ~10:10 ET; residual retries persisted in some long-running batch jobs.

Action for you: if you can temporarily reduce aggressive retry loops or add jitter for the next 2 hours, it will help clear queued retries on both sides. We can also open a quick 30-min bridge to walk through traces if helpful — available 13:30 ET today.

Attached: high-level runbook (redwood_incident_runbook_v1.pdf). I'll follow up with a CSV timeline and traces export.

Thanks for your patience.

Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 16:45:00 -0400
Subject: Post-incident summary: 2025-06-18 us-east-1 elevated 503s (SprintBridge)

Hi Sophie / Alex —

Thank you for working with us on this. Below is the post-incident summary and next steps. Please treat the attached timeline and traces as confidential.

Summary (one-paragraph):
On 2025-06-18 at ~08:40 ET we observed a rapid series of KV cache shard evictions in us-east-1 that caused increased cold starts for long-context model sessions. Our circuit-breaker protections returned 503s to contain load, which affected SprintBridge batch ingestion. Our SREs applied forced warmup and an expanded prefetch window, and rerouted a portion of traffic to burst pools; request success rates returned to baseline by ~11:10 ET.

Root cause: An interaction between a GC spike on a subset of cache hosts and a rate of long-context session spikes exceeded our prefetch/warmup heuristics, triggering cascading evictions. We are tracking a code fix to prevent simultaneous eviction amplification during GC events.

Customer impact: intermittent 503s for ~2.5 hours, increased retries on batch jobs, delayed downstream ingestion. No data loss observed.

Corrective actions (short/medium/long):
- Short: Adjust circuit-breaker thresholds and extend automated prefetch window for long-context sessions during high eviction signals (completed 2025-06-18).
- Medium: Operationalize a targeted warm cache reserve for customers with heavy long-context workloads in us-east-1 (ETA: 2025-07-08).
- Long: Root-cause patch to cache host GC behavior and improved eviction coordination logic (ETA: 2025-07-22).

Attachments: incident-timeline-20250618.csv (detailed trace times), redwood_incident_runbook_v1.pdf (mitigation steps and recommended customer-side retry guidance).

If you'd like a walkthrough of the traces or to coordinate specific threshold changes for SprintBridge, we can set time next week. Apologies again for the disruption and thank you for your patience.

Best regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
